Definition: a diminutive of G975; a booklet:--little book.
BiblicalUsage: The little book is the small scroll in the angel's hand in Revelation 10, and John is told to take it and eat it. In Revelation 10:2 the mighty angel holds the little book open, in Revelation 10:9 John takes it and eats it, and in Revelation 10:10 it is sweet in his mouth and bitter in his belly. The word is the diminutive of book — a little book with a great message. Note: the text spells it βιβλαρίδιον, with the letters in a different order from the dictionary form, but it is the same word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the little book is the whole prophetic calling in miniature: sweet to receive, bitter to carry, and not to be left unread.
